Dedicated Mac vs shared or virtual cloud Mac: how to choose

Reviewed: 2026-11-21 · WodeMac

If you need a Mac that stays online, keeps its environment, gives you admin rights and a full desktop, a dedicated physical Mac fits better. If you only run occasional builds and are happy starting from a clean environment each time, an on-demand shared or virtual macOS service may cost less. Providers differ a lot, so check each point against your own project rather than comparing prices alone.

The common kinds of cloud macOS

  • Dedicated physical Mac: a whole Mac rented to one customer, billed per month or year, with an environment that persists. WodeMac is in this category.
  • Shared host: several users on the same Mac, each with an account, sharing the hardware.
  • On-demand virtual environment: macOS virtual machines or build environments created on Apple hardware when needed, common in hosted build services; the environment may be discarded when the job ends.

These are general differences between categories. For any specific provider, resources, permissions and billing are whatever that provider states.

Side by side

ItemDedicated physical MacShared or virtual macOS
HardwareAll CPU, memory and storage are yoursShared with other users or environments, usually with quotas
PersistenceLong-lived; tools and caches stay installedDepends on the service; some start fresh each time
Admin rightsYesDepends on the service; may be limited
Graphical desktopFull desktopDepends on the service; some offer only a command line or build interface
BillingFixed per period, independent of usageOften by usage or by time

When a dedicated Mac makes sense

  • You develop, debug and build on it every day and want Xcode, simulators, dependencies and caches to stay put.
  • You need admin rights to install and configure tools, certificates and your environment.
  • You need a full desktop, for example to test an app by hand in the simulator.
  • Your team wants one Mac per person, with projects, permissions and data kept apart.
  • You want a fixed monthly cost that is easy to budget.

When on-demand or shared is enough

  • You run builds or tests only now and then, and the machine would sit idle most of the time.
  • Your pipeline is designed to start from a clean environment and keeps no state.
  • You do not need a desktop or admin rights.

In that case a pay-per-use service may cost less. You can also combine them: a dedicated Mac for daily development and an on-demand service for occasional bursts of jobs.

Questions to ask any provider

  1. Is it a whole physical machine, a shared machine or a virtual machine?
  2. Are all the CPU, memory and storage mine, or is there a quota?
  3. Do I get admin rights and a desktop? Will the environment be reset?
  4. Who else can access the machine, and why?
  5. How is it billed, how fast is delivery, and what happens to my data at the end?

For WodeMac: a whole M6 Mac mini rented to one customer, with admin rights and a full desktop; WodeMac and the hosting provider keep admin access for maintenance; paid upfront per period; delivery usually within 24 hours and no later than 3 business days.

FAQ

Is a dedicated Mac always faster than a virtual one?

Not necessarily; it depends on the hardware, quotas and load. The advantage of a dedicated machine is that its resources are not shared with anyone. The reliable test is building your own project on it.

Is a shared or virtual macOS service always cheaper?

No. Pay-per-use can be cheaper for occasional work; for long daily use, a fixed-price dedicated machine is often easier to budget. Compare against your real usage.

Which kind is WodeMac?

A dedicated physical Mac. Each M6 Mac mini is rented to one customer and is not a virtual machine. WodeMac and the hosting provider keep admin access for maintenance.
